40f2edc feat: sync-template now shows total diff with NEW/existing separation [90m(27/12/2025)[0m
  BREAKING CHANGE: sync-template behavior changed to support incremental syncing
  
  Previous behavior (BROKEN):
  - Only showed changes since last sync
  - If you applied partial changes, unapplied changes were lost
  - "No new template commits" blocked seeing existing differences
  
  New behavior (FIXED):
  - Always shows TOTAL diff (current state vs current state)
  - Separates changes into:
    * NEW since last sync (highlighted)
    * Existing differences (greyed out)
  - Supports incremental workflow:
    1. Apply safe changes first
    2. Come back later for conflicts
    3. Never lose track of unapplied changes
  
  Display changes:
  - "Safe changes - NEW since last sync" (normal color)
  - "Safe changes - existing differences" (grey)
  - "Conflicts - NEW since last sync" (normal color)
  - "Conflicts - existing differences" (grey)
  
  This matches --diff-summary behavior and enables proper incremental syncing.
  
  🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
  
  Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

47423a8 feat: add --modified-only flag to sync-template diff-summary [90m(27/12/2025)[0m
  Adds a new --modified-only option to show only files that differ from the
  template, excluding:
  - New files (in template but not in project)
  - Ignored files (matching ignoredFiles patterns)
  - Project-specific files (matching projectSpecificFiles patterns)
  
  This is useful for reviewing what has changed in existing shared files
  without the noise of project-specific customizations or new template features.
  
  Usage:
    yarn sync-template --diff-summary --modified-only
  
  The output will show only the "Modified" section with diffs of files that
  exist in both the template and project but have diverged.
  
  🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

1aa9369 fix: loading states showing false empty state before data loads [90m(27/12/2025)[0m
  CRITICAL UX FIX: Components were showing 'No items' empty state while
  data was still loading, confusing users with false empty states.
  
  Changes:
  - Fix Todos.tsx to check loading state before showing empty state
  - Add 'Loading States - CRITICAL UX Pattern' section to:
    - app-guildelines/React-components-guidelines.md
    - docs/state-management.md
    - docs/caching-strategy.md
    - .cursor/rules/react-component-organization.mdc
  
  The correct pattern is: Loading → Error → Empty → Data
  - isLoading=true && !data → Loading spinner
  - error → Error message
  - !data → Unable to load
  - data.length === 0 → Empty state (ONLY when truly empty)
  - data.length > 0 → Show data

d43a026 fix(ios): simplify - replace 500 lines with scroll jiggle workaround [90m(2025-12-23)[0m
  The previous approach was overengineered. This simple fix:
  1. When keyboard closes (focusout on input)
  2. Do a tiny scroll jiggle (+1px then back)
  3. This forces iOS to recalculate its viewport
  
  ~500 lines → ~90 lines. Sometimes simple is better.

4951b82 fix(ios): always apply offset in iOS quirk mode, remove vv_offsetTop check [90m(2025-12-23)[0m
  Root cause: vv_offsetTop fluctuates between 0 and >0 during iOS scroll
  animations, causing rapid offset toggling (flickering navbar).
  
  Fix: Once in iOS quirk mode (vv_height < innerHeight by ~68px), always
  apply the 68px offset. This works for both scroll=0 (home indicator
  visible) and scrolled states (navbar lifted into view). The previous
  vv_offsetTop check was the source of the flickering.

8b40576 fix(ios): check vv_offsetTop to determine if offset needed when scrolled [90m(2025-12-23)[0m
  Root cause: After keyboard closes in iOS PWA, when at scroll=0 the
  navbar is visible in the home indicator area (vv_offsetTop=0). But
  when scrolled DOWN, iOS shifts the visual viewport (vv_offsetTop=68)
  and the navbar gets pushed below visible area.
  
  Fix: Check vv_offsetTop - only apply offset when scrolled (offsetTop > 0).
  At scroll=0 (offsetTop=0), CSS safe area handles positioning.

dba4a53 fix(ios): use threshold instead of safe area for keyboard detection [90m(2025-12-23)[0m
  The iOS viewport quirk after keyboard closes is ~68px, not equal to
  safeAreaBottom (34px). Use a 100px threshold to distinguish between
  iOS quirks (should be 0 offset) vs real keyboard/toolbar (needs offset).
94adca7 fix: revert yarn.lock to fix build [90m(2025-12-23)[0m

ce0978c fix(ios): prevent double-compensation for safe area inset [90m(2025-12-23)[0m
  Root cause: After keyboard closes in iOS PWA mode, visualViewport.height
  is 68px smaller than innerHeight due to the home indicator safe area.
  Our calculation saw this as a 68px offset, but CSS already handles
  safe area via paddingBottom: env(safe-area-inset-bottom).
  
  Fix: Measure safe-area-inset-bottom and subtract it from the calculated
  offset to prevent double-compensation. When offset equals safe area
  (and keyboard is not active), set offset to 0.
